extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary and secondary education administrators, Title IX coordinators, institutional legal counsel, and policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to the Department of Education's Title IX final rule explaining definitions and procedural requirements for complaints and grievance procedures, including who qualifies as a complainant and how recipients must handle complaints. Focus is on implementing and interpreting regulatory provisions (e.g., §§106.1–106.2, §106.45) in institutional compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Administrative Law Judge' (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised definition of 'administrative law judge' specifically refers and applies to a hearing held under §106.81, which pertains to the Department's efforts to secure a recipient's compliance with Title IX, and is distinct from hearings that may be conducted as part of a recipient's Title IX grievance procedures under §§106.45 or 106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the definition does not require a hearing for all Title IX grievance procedures; a hearing under §106.81 is distinct from recipient-conducted grievance hearings and does not imply ALJ involvement in §§106.45/106.46 processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad definition of 'Complainant'
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits a complaint by someone who is not currently a student or employee as long as that person was participating or attempting to participate in a recipient's education program or activity at the time of the alleged discrimination; the proposed definition did not include the term 'victim'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: prevents exclusion of prospective students, former students, and former employees who were participating or attempting to participate at time of alleged discrimination; encourages reporting given delayed disclosure patterns; omitting 'victim' avoids stigmatizing language. Recipients should treat such complaints under their grievance procedures consistent with §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of 'participating or attempting to participate' — assessed at time of alleged discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether someone is 'participating or attempting to participate' is assessed at the time of the alleged sex discrimination (not at the time the complaint is filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a fact-specific, case-by-case determination. Examples: prospective students visiting campus, guest speakers, visiting student-athletes, campus-tour attendees, and others can be complainants if the alleged discrimination relates to their participation or attempted participation. The Department rejects narrowing to 'applying' as too limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must provide prompt and equitable grievance procedures for all sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require recipients to adopt grievance procedures that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of all complaints of sex discrimination—not limited to sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with Title IX's purpose to eliminate discrimination on the basis of sex in any education program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance. Recipients must ensure grievance procedures cover all forms of sex discrimination and take steps to provide an educational environment free from sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal standards and elimination of vague 'specific circumstances' dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposed removing §106.45(b)(3)(ii) (which allowed dismissal when 'specific circumstances' prevent gathering sufficient evidence) and instead revised the dismissal standard to include several defined bases for discretionary dismissal (e.g., respondent not participating/employed, allegations would not constitute sex discrimination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, at the time the complaint is filed, the respondent is no longer participating in the recipient's program or employed, the complaint may be dismissed under §106.45(d)(1)(ii). Recipients also may dismiss under §106.45(d)(iv) if allegations, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retroactivity of final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department intends the final regulations to be enforced prospectively and not retroactively; agencies may only issue retroactive rules if the authorizing statute expressly grants such authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual who left an institution files a complaint seeking compliance solely with regulatory requirements that were not in effect at the time of the alleged conduct, the recipient would dismiss the complaint. This is grounded in APA and case law (e.g., Bowen v. Georgetown Univ. Hosp.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of former students, employees, and certain trainees as complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: Former students and employees who were participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity at the time of the alleged sex discrimination may be complainants; postdoctoral trainees/fellows might fall within the definition depending on facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should proceed with such complaints under normal grievance procedures (§106.45; §106.46 if applicable). The Department declines to make the provision retroactive and declines to explicitly enumerate postdoctoral trainees but recognizes they could be covered as students or employees depending on context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX protects 'persons' including volunteers and visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX protects all 'person[s]' from sex discrimination under a recipient's education program or activity, which can include volunteers and visitors participating or attempting to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects arguments that covering volunteers will hinder recruitment; ensuring volunteers can participate free from sex discrimination should aid recruitment and retention. Recipients are not legally obligated to initiate grievance procedures for persons having no relationship to the recipient absent the participation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department response to anticipated increase in complaints and associated burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department recognizes commenters' concerns that broader complainant definitions and other changes (e.g., removing actual knowledge standard, including gender identity, allowing off‑campus conduct) may increase complaints and administrative costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite potential increased volume and costs, the Department views ensuring full compliance with Title IX as paramount; it considered costs in the Regulatory Impact Analysis and concluded the benefits justify the burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying edits to regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical edits to definitions were made (e.g., adding 'or this part' after references to 'Title IX' and replacing phrasing with 'at the time of the alleged sex discrimination').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These edits aim to improve clarity and align the regulatory text with the interpretive discussion in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation requirement purpose and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The participation requirement was included to ensure complainants have a relationship to the recipient (participating or attempting to participate) and is not meant to limit recipients from offering supportive measures or explaining complaint processes to persons without such a relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should respond promptly (e.g., supportive measures) to reports even when the person is not a complainant for purposes of initiating formal grievance procedures, but they are not legally obligated to initiate grievance procedures for those with no relationship to the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example-based guidance from case law supporting broader complainant scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department cites appellate decisions (e.g., Doe v. Brown University; Snyder-Hill v. Ohio State Univ.) to illustrate that complainants include non‑students who were participating or attempting to participate when discrimination occurred (e.g., attending events, tours, camps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should consider precedent showing Title IX's scope extends to persons present for or attempting to access recipient programs/activities and apply fact-specific analyses accordingly.
